newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian senator sees Telstra sale mandate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian senator sees Telstra sale mandate.

text.p: Key Australian Independent Senator Mal Colston said on Thursday that the government had a mandate to sell a third of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp.
The government had won a big majority in the March election, in which the proposed sale was a feature, Colston told the Senate.
"It is hard to argue that the coalition did not obtain a mandate to sell one third of Telstra," he said, speaking in the debate on whether the Senate would pass the privatisation bill.
Colston said he had still to negotiate with the government for employment guarantees to secure his vote on the bill, although he expected a satisfactory result.

"In this respect I believe at this stage I am close to negotiating a satisfactory resolution in relation to employment opportunities for telephone operators in regional areas of Queensland (his home state)," he said.
So he would support the bill's immediate progress towards Senate passage but still had an opportunity to change his mind later, he said.
The government hopes for a final vote later on Thursday.

The government is two votes short of a majority in the Senate, the upper house of parliament, but all non-government senators except the two independents are opposed to selling a stake in Telstra, Australia's biggest company.
The other Independent is Brian Harradine, who said earlier that he could also support the bill, subject to his requirements being met.
